# REBUILD.md: rebuild guide for a white-label factory system

A complete, de-branded recipe for recreating a factory weighing, labelling, receiving and inventory system. It was written from the real project's files, with every company-specific name, address, colour, logo, product and person replaced by a placeholder (for example `{{COMPANY_NAME}}`) or by fictional sample data. A Claude instance (or a person) with no access to the original account can follow it from the top.

**Generated:** 2026-11-10 · **Files embedded:** 333 · **Size of this file:** 2.0 MB

## 0. How to use this file (read first)

This file is large because it holds the full text of every source file (about 2.0 MB). **Do not retype it.** It is built so that a small script can write all the files for you.

1. **Do not try to read the whole file in one go.** Read sections 0 to 10 first (they are short, roughly the first 200 lines). Part B (the file contents) starts at the line that says `# Part B`; read it only when you need a specific file.
2. **Copy the extractor** (section 0.1) into a file called `extract.mjs` next to this file.
3. **Choose the branding**: run the extractor once; it writes `rebuild.config.json` with sample values (a made-up company) and stops. Edit the values (section 8 explains each one), then run it again.
4. The extractor writes every file into the output folder, replaces every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` with the value from `rebuild.config.json`, and draws placeholder logos in the brand colours.
5. Continue with section 9 (install, database baseline, tests, run).

```bash
node extract.mjs REBUILD.md ./system rebuild.config.json
```

Rules for the values in `rebuild.config.json`: no double quotes, single quotes, backslashes, backticks, dollar signs or line breaks (they would break strings inside source files; use ’ instead of '). Colours are `#rrggbb`.

### 0.1 The extractor (`extract.mjs`)

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// extract.mjs: writes every file of REBUILD.md into a folder and fills in the {{PLACEHOLDERS}}.
// Usage: node extract.mjs [REBUILD.md] [output-folder] [rebuild.config.json]
// No packages needed. The first run creates rebuild.config.json (sample values) and stops, so you can
// edit the branding; the second run writes the project.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import zlib from "node:zlib";

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
if (args.includes("--help") || args.includes("-h")) {
  console.log("Usage: node extract.mjs [REBUILD.md] [output-folder] [rebuild.config.json]");
  process.exit(0);
}
const [specFile = "REBUILD.md", outDir = "./system", configFile = "rebuild.config.json"] = args;

const DEFAULTS = {
  "COMPANY_NAME": "Northfield Foods",
  "COMPANY_NAME_HE": "נורת׳פילד פודס",
  "COMPANY_FILE_PREFIX": "Northfield-Foods",
  "SYSTEM_NAME": "Northfield Foods - Factory",
  "SYSTEM_NAME_HE": "נורת׳פילד פודס - מפעל",
  "SENDER_NAME": "Northfield Foods System",
  "APP_ID": "northfield",
  "APP_URL": "https://app.example.com",
  "APP_HOST": "app.example.com",
  "COMPANY_DOMAIN": "example.com",
  "OWNER_EMAIL": "owner@example.com",
  "OWNER_NAME": "Alex Owner",
  "SMTP_FROM_ADDRESS": "system@example.com",
  "RENDER_SERVICE_NAME": "northfield-factory",
  "RENDER_DB_NAME": "northfield-db",
  "QR_PREFIX": "NF",
  "BRAND_COLOR": "#1f6f78",
  "BRAND_COLOR_ALT": "#1a5f68",
  "ACCENT_COLOR": "#b8862b",
  "ACCENT_COLOR_LIGHT": "#e2b866",
  "ACCENT_COLOR_SOFT": "#f7edd8"
};

// ---- the values
if (!fs.existsSync(configFile)) {
  fs.writeFileSync(configFile, JSON.stringify(DEFAULTS, null, 2) + "\n");
  console.log(`Wrote ${configFile} with sample values for a made-up company.`);
  console.log("Edit it (see section 8 of REBUILD.md), then run the same command again.");
  process.exit(0);
}
const config = { ...DEFAULTS, ...JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(configFile, "utf8")) };
// Derived values (not in the config file).
config.QR_PREFIX_LOWER = String(config.QR_PREFIX ?? "").toLowerCase();
for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(config)) {
  if (key === "QR_PREFIX_LOWER") continue;
  if (typeof value !== "string" || value === "" || /["'\\`$\n\r{}]/.test(value)) {
    throw new Error(`${configFile}: the value of ${key} must be a non-empty text without quotes, backslashes, backticks, $, braces or line breaks`);
  }
  if (key.includes("COLOR") && !/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/.test(value)) {
    throw new Error(`${configFile}: ${key} must be a colour like #1f6f78`);
  }
}

// ---- read the files out of REBUILD.md
const lines = fs.readFileSync(specFile, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").split("\n");
const files = [];
for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
  const heading = /^### FILE: `([^`]+)`\s*$/.exec(lines[i]);
  if (!heading) continue;
  let j = i + 1;
  while (lines[j] === "") j++;
  const fence = /^(`{4,})(\S*)\s*$/.exec(lines[j] ?? "");
  if (!fence) throw new Error(`no code block after the heading of ${heading[1]} (line ${i + 1})`);
  const body = [];
  for (j++; j < lines.length && lines[j] !== fence[1]; j++) body.push(lines[j]);
  if (j >= lines.length) throw new Error(`the code block of ${heading[1]} is not closed`);
  files.push({ path: heading[1], text: body.join("\n") + "\n" });
  i = j;
}
if (files.length === 0) throw new Error(`no files found in ${specFile}`);

// ---- write them, with the placeholders filled in
let written = 0;
for (const file of files) {
  const text = file.text.replace(/\{\{([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\}\}/g, (all, key) => {
    if (!(key in config)) throw new Error(`${file.path}: unknown placeholder ${all}; add it to ${configFile}`);
    return config[key];
  });
  const target = path.join(outDir, file.path);
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(target), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(target, text);
  written++;
}

// ---- placeholder pictures (simple shapes in the brand colours; replace with the real artwork)
const crcTable = Array.from({ length: 256 }, (_, n) => {
  let c = n;
  for (let k = 0; k < 8; k++) c = c & 1 ? 0xedb88320 ^ (c >>> 1) : c >>> 1;
  return c >>> 0;
});
const crc32 = (buf) => {
  let crc = 0xffffffff;
  for (const byte of buf) crc = crcTable[(crc ^ byte) & 0xff] ^ (crc >>> 8);
  return (crc ^ 0xffffffff) >>> 0;
};
const chunk = (type, data) => {
  const body = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(type), data]);
  const out = Buffer.alloc(8 + data.length + 4);
  out.writeUInt32BE(data.length, 0);
  body.copy(out, 4);
  out.writeUInt32BE(crc32(body), 8 + data.length);
  return out;
};
const rgb = (hex) => [1, 3, 5].map((i) => parseInt(hex.slice(i, i + 2), 16));

/** shapes: [{ kind: "rect"|"circle", box: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in 0..1, color: [r,g,b,a] }], drawn in order */
function png(width, height, background, shapes) {
  const raw = Buffer.alloc((width * 4 + 1) * height);
  for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) {
    raw[y * (width * 4 + 1)] = 0;
    for (let x = 0; x < width; x++) {
      let pixel = background;
      for (const shape of shapes) {
        const [x0, y0, x1, y1] = shape.box;
        const u = x / width;
        const v = y / height;
        const inside =
          shape.kind === "rect"
            ? u >= x0 && u <= x1 && v >= y0 && v <= y1
            : ((u - (x0 + x1) / 2) / ((x1 - x0) / 2)) ** 2 + ((v - (y0 + y1) / 2) / ((y1 - y0) / 2)) ** 2 <= 1;
        if (inside) pixel = shape.color;
      }
      raw.set(pixel, y * (width * 4 + 1) + 1 + x * 4);
    }
  }
  const header = Buffer.alloc(13);
  header.writeUInt32BE(width, 0);
  header.writeUInt32BE(height, 4);
  header.set([8, 6, 0, 0, 0], 8);
  return Buffer.concat([
    Buffer.from([0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a]),
    chunk("IHDR", header),
    chunk("IDAT", zlib.deflateSync(raw)),
    chunk("IEND", Buffer.alloc(0)),
  ]);
}

const brand = [...rgb(config.BRAND_COLOR), 255];
const accent = [...rgb(config.ACCENT_COLOR), 255];
const ivory = [250, 246, 238, 255];
const white = [255, 255, 255, 255];
const clear = [0, 0, 0, 0];
const wordmark = (ink, dot) => [
  { kind: "circle", box: [0.08, 0.2, 0.32, 0.8], color: dot },
  { kind: "rect", box: [0.4, 0.38, 0.92, 0.62], color: ink },
];
const pictures = [
  ["public/brand/logo-light.png", png(1000, 500, clear, wordmark(ivory, accent))],
  ["public/brand/logo.png", png(1000, 500, white, wordmark(brand, accent))],
  ["public/brand/logo-mark.png", png(320, 320, clear, [{ kind: "circle", box: [0.1, 0.1, 0.9, 0.9], color: brand }, { kind: "circle", box: [0.38, 0.38, 0.62, 0.62], color: white }])],
  ["src/app/icon.png", png(320, 320, brand, [{ kind: "circle", box: [0.25, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75], color: white }])],
  ["src/app/apple-icon.png", png(512, 512, brand, [{ kind: "circle", box: [0.25, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75], color: white }])],
  ["src/app/opengraph-image.png", png(600, 600, ivory, [{ kind: "circle", box: [0.2, 0.2, 0.8, 0.8], color: brand }, { kind: "circle", box: [0.4, 0.4, 0.6, 0.6], color: accent }])],
];
for (const [file, bytes] of pictures) {
  const target = path.join(outDir, file);
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(target), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(target, bytes);
}

console.log(`Wrote ${written} files and ${pictures.length} placeholder pictures into ${outDir}`);
console.log("Next: cd " + outDir + " && corepack enable && pnpm install   (see section 9 of REBUILD.md)");
````

### 0.2 How Part B is laid out

Each file is a heading of the form `### FILE: \`path/to/file`` followed by a fenced block (four or more backticks, as many as needed so that the file's own backticks never close it). The extractor reads the headings in order. A file's text between the fences is exactly the file, de-branded. If you prefer to create a file by hand, copy the text between the fences.

## 1. Overview

### 1.1 What the system does (generic terms)

A browser application for a food factory that sits beside the company's ERP (called **Priority** in this build; it is an Israeli ERP with an OData API, and everything about it is isolated behind one interface so another ERP can be added). It:

* **Prints labels.** A visual **label designer** (drag, resize, fields, barcodes, QR codes, logo, ready-made sections) edits layouts in millimetres. Item labels are printed from the catalog; a box label is printed for every weighed box; pallet labels summarise a pallet; **shipping labels** are printed for orders that the ERP sends.
* **Receives goods.** *Goods receiving*: scan the item label's QR code, put the box on a connected scale (read directly by the browser over the Web Serial API, or a simulated scale), save the box and print its barcode label. *Vendor receiving*: scan the 30-digit barcode that a vendor printed on the box; scans are queued, three sounds tell the result.
* **Sends every box to the ERP** as its own line, through a send queue with retries (a box is always saved locally first). Writing is gated by an environment variable.
* **Shows stock.** A dashboard (warehouse cards, expiry warnings, per-user room order), and an inventory screen down to a single box (filters, Excel and PDF reports, pallets built by ticking or scanning boxes).
* **Shipping labels.** The ERP calls a secret URL when an order is picked and confirmed; the order is kept and its labels are printed numbered "Box 1 of 10" (or "Pallet 1 of 10", with several labels per pallet number).
* **Controls access.** Users with per-screen and per-action permissions, per-device permissions (desktop or phone), password plus optional Google sign-in and TOTP two-factor, an activity log that is never edited, security alerts, an administrator inbox for messages from users, and a built-in help window on every page with an optional AI question helper that answers from the user manual.
* **Hebrew first, English second**, with right-to-left layout done through logical CSS classes.
* **Documents itself**: a user manual (PDF, English and Hebrew) built from the real screens by a Playwright picture-taking script.

### 1.2 How the parts connect

```
Browser (desktop at the factory, or phone)
  │   Next.js App Router pages (React 19, server components + client components)
  │   Server actions for every write; a few route handlers under /api
  ▼
Next.js server  (src/proxy.ts: cookie check; pages verify the session for real)
  │   src/server/*  business modules (permissions, receiving, labels, pallets, shipping-labels, ...)
  │   src/lib/*     pure code shared by browser and server (barcodes, label model, formats)
  ▼
Drizzle ORM ──► PostgreSQL (embedded PGlite in development/tests, a real Postgres in production)
  │
  └── Priority client (src/server/priority): fake (tables fake_priority_*) | live (OData over HTTPS)
        send worker (src/server/receiving/worker.ts) drains the queue to the ERP
```

* **Auth:** Better Auth (email + password, optional Google, TOTP two-factor), database sessions, a per-device-type permission, idle logout.
* **i18n:** next-intl; `messages/he.json` and `messages/en.json` hold all texts (dot-free keys; dynamic keys need `as never`).
* **Labels:** layouts are rows in `label_layouts` (JSON elements). Printing renders the label at exact millimetres into a hidden copy of the page and calls `window.print()` with an `@page` size; it works with any printer, and with a kiosk-printing shortcut it prints silently.
* **Priority stand-in:** by default (`PRIORITY_MODE=fake`) a sample ERP is simulated inside the database, so the system runs with no ERP at all (this is what a demo uses).
* **Tests:** about 300 unit tests (Vitest, in-memory PGlite) and about 120 browser tests (Playwright, against a production build with its own embedded database). The e2e files are numbered and must run in order (they share state).
* **Manual:** `manual/` holds the text (English and Hebrew), a picture-taking script and a PDF builder; `manual/make-knowledge.mjs` turns the manual text into `src/server/assistant/knowledge.ts` for the question helper.

### 1.3 Technology

TypeScript, Next.js 16 (App Router, `cacheComponents` off), React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui on Base UI (RTL preset), next-intl, Drizzle + PostgreSQL 17 (PGlite for development), Better Auth, Zod, Vitest, Playwright, pnpm. Node 24 is used for hosting (22+ works locally).

**AGENTS.md note:** the project uses a Next.js version with breaking changes; `AGENTS.md` tells coding agents to read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing code. Keep that file.

### 2.2 Files that are not embedded (and how to get them)

|What|Why it is not embedded|How it is produced|
|-|-|-|
|`pnpm-lock.yaml`|300 KB machine-written lock file|`pnpm install` writes it|
|`src/server/db/migrations/**` (SQL, journal, snapshots)|Generated from `schema.ts`; the original history belongs to the original company's database|`pnpm db:generate` writes a fresh baseline migration `0000_*.sql` from the final schema (section 9, step 6)|
|`src/server/assistant/knowledge.ts`|Generated from the manual text|`node manual/make-knowledge.mjs` (section 9, step 7)|
|`manual/shots/**`, `Manual PDF/**`|Pictures and PDFs generated from the running system|`pnpm exec playwright test -c manual/playwright.config.ts`, then `node manual/build.mjs`|
|`node_modules`, `.next*`, `data/`, `test-results/`, `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`|Build output|`pnpm install`, `pnpm build`|
|`.env.local`|Holds secrets|Create it from `.env.example` (section 4)|

## 3. Custom skills, agents, slash commands, hooks and plugins

The original project defines **none** of these. Specifically, after inspecting the project folder and the account's configuration:

* **Skills / SKILL.md:** none in the project (`.claude/skills` does not exist).
* **Agents (`.claude/agents`):** none.
* **Slash commands (`.claude/commands`):** none.
* **Hooks:** none (no `hooks` entry in any settings file).
* **Plugins:** none installed for this project (only a built-in plugin that reads `AGENTS.md`).
* **`CLAUDE.md`:** none. The only agent instruction file is `AGENTS.md` (the Next.js notice; its full text is in Part B).
* **Project Claude config:** a single file, `.claude/launch.json`, which tells the desktop app how to start preview servers (its full text is in Part B):

  * `dev` → `pnpm dev` on port 3000 (the development server with the embedded database)
  * `remote` → `node scripts/serve-remote.mjs` on port 3001 (the production build against the running dev database, for opening the system from another computer)

Nothing needs to be created for this section. If you want your own conventions for the rebuilt system, add a `CLAUDE.md` with the content of section 7.

## 4. Settings

### 4.1 Claude settings and permissions

* **Project `settings.json` / `settings.local.json`:** none exist. No allow-list, no deny-list, no hooks, no environment overrides.
* **User-level settings:** one preference only (agent push notifications on), which is personal and not part of the system.
* **Permissions:** the work was done in the desktop app's normal permission mode, asking for approval of shell commands and file edits. To reduce prompts in the new account, an owner may allow read-only commands such as `pnpm test`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `git status` and `git diff`; this is a convenience, not a requirement.

### 4.2 MCP servers and connectors

The system **does not require any MCP server or connector**. While building it, only the desktop app's built-in tools were used: the built-in browser pane (to look at the running app), optionally the Claude in Chrome extension, the terminal tools, and the scheduled-tasks tool. No scopes, tokens or server configuration are needed to rebuild the system. There is no `.mcp.json`.

### 4.3 Environment variables

Create `.env.local` from `.env.example` (its full text is in Part B). All secrets are placeholders; **never commit real values**.

|Variable|Used for|Notes|
|-|-|-|
|`DATABASE_URL`|PostgreSQL connection|Empty = embedded PGlite in `./data/pglite`. Production: the Postgres connection string.|
|`DATABASE_POOL_MAX`|Connection pool size|Optional|
|`APP_URL`|Public address (auth callbacks, emails, `metadataBase`)|`http://localhost:3000` locally; `{{APP_URL}}` in production|
|`TRUSTED_ORIGINS`|Other addresses allowed in development (a phone on the same Wi-Fi)|Optional, comma separated|
|`AUTH_SECRET`|Signs sessions; also the key for encrypting stored secrets|Required. Generate: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`. Changing it makes stored secrets unreadable.|
|`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`|Google sign-in|Optional; empty hides the button|
|`PRIORITY_MODE`|`fake` (built-in sample ERP) or `live`|Use `fake` for demos|
|`PRIORITY_WRITE`|`on` allows writing boxes to the live ERP|Only with `PRIORITY_MODE=live`|
|`SEED_OWNER_EMAIL`, `SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD`, `SEED_OWNER_NAME`|The owner account created on the first start (when there are no users)|The owner must change the password at first sign-in|
|`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_FROM`|Email with sign-in details for new users|Optional|
|`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`|The AI question helper in the help window|Optional; without it the tab says the helper is off|
|`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`|A different model / endpoint for the helper|Optional (the manual's picture script points the base URL at a local fake)|
|`PGLITE_DIR`, `PGLITE_PORT`|Where the embedded database lives / the port of its server in `pnpm dev`|Defaults `./data/pglite`, `54329`|
|`NEXT_DIST_DIR`|Separate build folder (used by the browser tests and the manual)|e.g. `.next-e2e`|
|`E2E_RELAXED_RATE_LIMIT`, `E2E_DEV`|Browser-test switches|Test only|
|`NODE_VERSION`|Render's Node version|`24`|

## 5. Dependencies

* **Runtime:** Node.js 24 (22 or newer works locally) and **pnpm 12.14.0** (`corepack enable` then `corepack prepare pnpm@12.14.0 --activate`, or `npm i -g pnpm`).
* **Language:** TypeScript 5.
* **Packages:** exactly as in `package.json` (full text in Part B). Notable runtime packages: `next 16.4.2`, `react 19.3.0`, `better-auth`, `drizzle-orm`, `@electric-sql/pglite 0.5.11`, `pg`, `next-intl`, `zod 4`, `bwip-js` (barcodes and QR), `write-excel-file 4.1.1`, `nodemailer`, `lucide-react`, `sonner`, `shadcn`. Dev: `vitest 5`, `@playwright/test`, `drizzle-kit`, `tailwindcss 4`, `eslint 9`, `prettier`, `tsx`, `pdfjs-dist 4.10.38`.
* **Overrides:** `pnpm-workspace.yaml` pins `@swc/core` to 1.16.0 (explained inside the file) and disables a few install scripts.
* **Browser for tests and the manual:** Playwright's Chromium: `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`.

Install commands:

```bash
corepack enable
pnpm install
pnpm exec playwright install chromium   # only for e2e tests and the manual
```

## 6. External services, scheduled tasks, manual setup

**Scheduled tasks:** none (no scheduled tasks or cron routines exist; the application's only background job is the in-process send worker that retries sending boxes to the ERP).

|Service|Needed?|What to set up by hand|
|-|-|-|
|**Hosting (Render blueprint in `render.yaml`)**|For a public demo|Create a Render account; connect the Git repository; apply the blueprint (one web service, one PostgreSQL 17 database, region of your choice). Set the `sync: false` variables (`APP_URL`, `SEED_OWNER_EMAIL`, `SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD`, `SEED_OWNER_NAME`) in the dashboard. Auto-deploy happens on every push. Any host that runs Node and Postgres works.|
|**Git hosting (GitHub)**|Recommended|Create a repository for the new system. Do not reuse the original repository.|
|**The ERP (Priority)**|No for demos|Demos run on the built-in stand-in (`PRIORITY_MODE=fake`). A real connection is entered in System settings → Priority (address, API user key, password; stored encrypted). Writes also need `PRIORITY_WRITE=on` and an API user with write permission.|
|**Google sign-in**|No|Create an OAuth client in Google Cloud for the new domain; set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`.|
|**Email (SMTP)**|No|Any SMTP account (for Gmail use `smtp.gmail.com`, port 465 and an app password).|
|**Anthropic API**|No|Create a key in the new Anthropic account and set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to enable the question helper.|
|**Domain name**|No|Point it at the host and set `APP_URL`.|
|**Hardware**|No|A USB barcode scanner (types into the focused field), a label printer set as the default printer (a kiosk-printing shortcut of Chrome/Edge makes printing silent), and optionally a scale on a serial/USB port read by Chrome or Edge (Web Serial). A simulated scale exists for demos.|
|**Google Fonts**|Automatic|`next/font` downloads the fonts at build time (needs internet during `pnpm build`).|

## 7. Memory and context

The original account had no saved memory entries and no `CLAUDE.md`. What Claude relied on were instructions the owner gave in conversation. They are reproduced here, de-branded, as working agreements. Save them as `CLAUDE.md` in the new project if you want the same behaviour.

```markdown
# Working agreements for this project

- The person who owns the system is not a developer. Explain things in short, plain words, one step at a time, say plainly what was and was not verified, and do the work for them.
- The interface is Hebrew first (right to left) with English as the second language. Use logical CSS classes (start/end, ps/pe) only. New texts go into both messages/he.json and messages/en.json.
- Commit and push only when the owner says so explicitly ("Commit and push"). Do not change anything outside the project folder without asking. Ask before anything that needs a password or a sign-in. Never enter, repeat or store passwords, keys or payment details; secrets are typed by the owner into the settings screen or the hosting dashboard.
- Before changing Next.js code, read the relevant guide in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ (this Next.js version has breaking changes; see AGENTS.md).
- Always run the whole browser-test suite (`pnpm exec playwright test --reporter=line`, about 6 minutes), never a subset: the tests share state and later files depend on earlier ones.
- Keep unit tests (`pnpm test`), `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` and lint clean before offering a change.
- When the manual's pictures or text change, regenerate the manual (pictures, `node manual/make-knowledge.mjs`, `node manual/build.mjs`) in both languages.
- Dynamic next-intl keys need `as never`; message keys contain no dots.
- Do not guess field names against a live ERP; ask for the real names.
```

Project knowledge that is not obvious from the code: the box barcode is 24 digits (25 with a 5-digit item number): running number (4) + item digits (4 or 5) + slaughter date (DDMMYY) + expiry date (DDMMYY) + net weight (4 digits, kg×100); vendor barcodes start with `38` and have 30 digits; the item label's QR is `{{QR_PREFIX}}1|<item>|<certificate>|<slaughter>|<production>|<expiry>` and a pallet's QR is `{{QR_PREFIX}}P1|<number>`; the list of today's boxes resets at 21:00.

* **Hebrew/English texts** in `messages/*.json` and the manual: neutral, but written for a food factory (slaughter date, expiry date, storage rooms). Edit them for another industry.

* **Logos and icons**: see 2.3.
* **Storage-room names** (the stand-in warehouses) in `db/seed/priority/warehouses.json`.
* **Priority** is the ERP integrated here; a different ERP needs a new client implementing `PriorityClient` (`src/server/priority/types.ts`).

## 9. Step-by-step rebuild order

Each step ends with a check. Do not continue until the check passes.

1. **Prepare the machine.** Install Node 24 (22+ works) and pnpm 12.14.0. Create an empty folder `my-system/`, put `REBUILD.md` in it.
*Check:* `node --version` prints v22 or newer; `pnpm --version` prints a version.
2. **Create the extractor.** Copy the script from section 0.1 into `extract.mjs`.
*Check:* `node extract.mjs --help` prints the usage line.
3. **Choose the branding.** Run `node extract.mjs REBUILD.md ./system rebuild.config.json`. The first run writes `rebuild.config.json` and stops; edit it (section 8) and run the same command again.
*Check:* the command ends with "Wrote N files" and `./system/package.json` exists.
4. **Look at the result.** `cd system`. Open `src/app/globals.css`.
*Check:* no placeholder remains: `grep -rIlE "{{[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*}}" .` prints nothing. (Plain `{{` is normal: React writes `style={{ ... }}`.)
5. **Install.** `corepack enable && pnpm install`. If `corepack enable` fails with a permission error (it writes into the Node folder), run `npm i -g pnpm@12.14.0` instead, then `pnpm install`.
*Check:* the command finishes without errors and creates `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `node_modules`.
6. **Create the database baseline.** `pnpm db:generate` (no database needed). It writes `src/server/db/migrations/0000_*.sql` and a snapshot.
*Check:* the folder `src/server/db/migrations` now holds one `.sql` file with `CREATE TABLE` statements (users, boxes, label_layouts, shipping_orders, ...).
7. **Build the assistant’s knowledge.** `node manual/make-knowledge.mjs` (creates `src/server/assistant/knowledge.ts` from the manual text).
*Check:* the file exists and is large (about 100 KB).
8. **Type-check and unit-test.** `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --incremental false` then `pnpm test`.
*Check:* no type errors; all unit tests pass (about 300).
9. **Create the environment file.** `cp .env.example .env.local`; set `AUTH_SECRET` (section 4.3), `SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD`, and leave `PRIORITY_MODE=fake`.
*Check:* `.env.local` has a non-empty `AUTH_SECRET`.
10. **Run it.** `pnpm dev`, open `http://localhost:3000`, sign in as the owner (`SEED_OWNER_EMAIL` / `SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD`), choose a new password.
*Check:* you land on the dashboard with warehouse cards and sample boxes; the menu lists Dashboard, Item catalog, Goods receiving, Vendor receiving, Shipping labels, Inventory management, System settings, System administration; the language button switches Hebrew/English and the layout mirrors.
11. **Try the main flows.** Catalog → print an item label (the browser's print window opens). Goods receiving → type a label QR (copy the format from section 7) and weigh with the simulated scale. System settings → Company and labels → Shipping labels → Open the settings → copy the address → "Make a test order" → Shipping labels screen → print labels.
*Check:* each flow completes without an error message.
12. **Browser tests (optional, about 7 minutes).** `pnpm exec playwright install chromium` then `pnpm exec playwright test --reporter=line`. It builds the app, starts its own server on port 3100 with a throwaway database, and runs every file in order.
*Check:* all pass (a few are skipped by design).
13. **Replace the artwork.** Put the real logos at the paths in 2.3 (or upload them in System settings → Company and labels).
*Check:* the sign-in page and the side menu show the new logo.
14. **Build the manual (optional).** Start the practice server `sh manual/server.sh` (port 3100, about 2 minutes to build), run `pnpm exec playwright test -c manual/playwright.config.ts` for the pictures, stop the server, then `node manual/make-knowledge.mjs` and `node manual/build.mjs`.
*Check:* `Manual PDF/` holds an English and a Hebrew PDF.
15. **Deploy (optional).** Push to a new Git repository, apply `render.yaml` on Render, set the secrets in the dashboard, set `APP_URL`.
*Check:* `/login` on the public address answers 200 and sign-in works.

---

## 10. Final checklist

* [ ] `rebuild.config.json` has the new company's values and no `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` remains in the generated project (`grep -rIlE "{{[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*}}" .` prints nothing).
* [ ] `pnpm install`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm test` all succeed.
* [ ] The owner can sign in, is asked to change the password, and sees every screen.
* [ ] Hebrew and English both work; Hebrew mirrors the layout.
* [ ] An item label prints; a box can be received with the simulated scale; a vendor box barcode is accepted; the shipping address works (`POST` a JSON order to it, the order appears and its labels print numbered).
* [ ] The label designer opens and saves a layout; a test print works.
* [ ] A new user can be created with limited permissions and sees only those screens.
* [ ] The placeholder logos were replaced and the colours match the new brand.
* [ ] No real secret is stored in any file that is committed (`.env.local` is ignored by git).
* [ ] **No references to the original company remain.** Search the generated project and this document for the original name, its Hebrew spelling, its domain and its colours (see the search terms in the delivery note of the person who produced this file); there must be zero matches.

---

````
# Copy to .env.local and fill in. Never commit .env.local.

# Database. Leave empty to use the embedded Postgres (PGlite) stored in ./data/pglite.
# For a real Postgres (docker compose up -d): postgres://weighing:weighing@localhost:5432/weighing,
# then start the app with `pnpm dev:app` (`pnpm dev` always runs its own PGlite server).
DATABASE_URL=

# Public URL of the app (used for auth callbacks). Local dev:
APP_URL=http://localhost:3000

# Other addresses the app is opened from, comma separated (for example a phone on the same Wi-Fi):
# TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://192.168.1.20:3000

# Secret for signing sessions. Generate one: openssl rand -base64 32
AUTH_SECRET=

# Google sign-in (OAuth client for {{COMPANY_DOMAIN}}). Leave empty to hide the Google button.
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=

# Priority connection mode: "fake" (stand-in with sample data) or "live" (phase 6).
PRIORITY_MODE=fake

# Owner account created by the seed (first run only, when there are no users yet).
# The owner must change this password on first login.
SEED_OWNER_EMAIL={{OWNER_EMAIL}}
SEED_OWNER_PASSWORD=change-me-on-first-login
SEED_OWNER_NAME={{OWNER_NAME}}

# Email (optional). With these set, a new user gets the sign-in link and temporary password by email.
# For a Google account use smtp.gmail.com, port 465 and an "app password" (not the normal password).
# SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
# SMTP_PORT=465
# SMTP_USER={{SMTP_FROM_ADDRESS}}
# SMTP_PASSWORD=
# SMTP_FROM="{{SENDER_NAME}} <{{SMTP_FROM_ADDRESS}}>"

# Question helper (optional). With a key from your Anthropic account, the help window of every
# page answers questions from the manual. Without it the "Ask a question" tab says it is off.
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
# A different model than the default (a small, cheap one):
# ANTHROPIC_MODEL=
````

### FILE: `DESIGN.md`

````markdown
# Design and UI conventions

Short rules so every screen looks and behaves the same. The owner can review every token and component on `/design` (owner only, not in the menu).

## The idea

A calm, classic look, organized: warm paper, a dark menu, thin accent hairlines, the brand colour kept for actions, and a serif face for titles and numbers. Nothing shouts. Things settle into place. The user should feel at ease within a second of logging in.

This is deliberately **not** a copy of the previous system (dark navy, bright pink-red, very round cards). It keeps what worked there (a side menu at the reading start, cards, pop-ups in the middle of the screen) and changes the character.

### Tokens (`src/app/globals.css`)

| Token                    | Value                 | Use                                                                               |
| ------------------------ | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--background`           | `#f6f1e9`             | Page canvas (warm paper)                                                          |
| `--card`                 | `#fffefb`             | Cards, pop-ups, inputs                                                            |
| `--foreground`           | `#1e1b18`             | Text (warm charcoal)                                                              |
| `--muted-foreground`     | `#756b5f`             | Secondary text                                                                    |
| `--border` / `--input`   | `#e4dacb` / `#dcd0be` | Hairlines, fields                                                                 |
| `--primary`              | `{{BRAND_COLOR}}`             | Main actions, focus ring (brand colour)                                               |
| `--sidebar`              | `#25221f`             | Side menu, phone bar, welcome panel (warm charcoal, formerly bottle green)        |
| `--sidebar-primary`      | `{{ACCENT_COLOR_LIGHT}}`             | Accent on the green: active marker, icons                                          |
| `--gold` / `--gold-soft` | `{{ACCENT_COLOR}}` / `{{ACCENT_COLOR_SOFT}}` | Accent on paper: labels, icon rings, ornaments                                     |
| `--brand`                | `{{BRAND_COLOR_ALT}}`             | The logo's own colour                                                                |
| `--success` / `-soft`    | `#2f6f4e` / `#e8f2ea` | In date, connected, OK                                                            |
| `--warning` / `-soft`    | `#a8620a` / `#fcf1dc` | Expiring soon                                                                     |
| `--destructive`          | `#d92d20`             | Expired, errors                                                                   |
| `--info` / `-soft`       | `#2d5b86` / `#e8f0f7` | Neutral information                                                               |
| `--radius`               | `0.625rem`            | Base. Cards `rounded-2xl`, pop-ups `rounded-3xl`, buttons and inputs `rounded-lg` |

The brand primary and the expiry red are different reds on purpose, and **every status carries an icon and a label**, never colour alone. Use the `Badge` variants `success`, `warning`, `destructive`, `info`, `soft`.

### Type

- **Frank Ruhl Libre** (serif, Hebrew and Latin) for page titles, card titles, pop-up titles and the big numbers: `font-serif`, and `font-heading` already maps to it.
- **Heebo** for everything people read and type: forms, tables, buttons, menu.
- **Geist Mono** for barcodes and codes. Numbers use `tabular-nums`.
- Small accent labels (eyebrows, menu section names) are 11px, semibold, wide letter spacing.

### Motion

Calm and short. Page headers, stat tiles and cards use `.rise` (a 10px fade-up, 0.6s) with `style={{ "--i": n }}` to stagger them 80ms apart. `prefers-reduced-motion` turns it off. Colours and the menu width transition at 200ms. No bouncing, no spinners except while refreshing.

### Sizes

Buttons are sized for a touch screen on the factory floor: 40px by default, 48px (`size="lg"`) for the main action of a screen or pop-up, 36px small. Inputs are 44px. These are the sizes at full scale (phones and tablets).

**Desktop scale:** from 1024px width up, `html` is set to 80% (`globals.css`), so every `rem` size shrinks together, as if the browser were zoomed to 80%, and the layout still spreads across the full width (so a default button is about 32px there). The owner asked for this after comparing the app at 100% and 80% browser zoom. Keep sizes in `rem` (never `px`, except hairlines and shadows) so new screens follow the scale; the page width limit is `max-w-[117rem]` for the same reason. To make the whole app larger or smaller, change that one percentage.

## App shell

`src/components/shell`. Every screen after login is inside it.

- **Desktop (1024px and up):** a fixed dark menu at the reading start (right in Hebrew, left in English), 288px wide, collapsible to a 96px icon rail with a round handle on its edge, remembered in a cookie. The light logo on top, the screens in two labelled sections (**Operations**: dashboard, catalog, receiving, vendor receiving, inventory; **System**: settings, administration), and the user card (monogram, name, job title or "Owner", language, sign out) at the bottom. The active entry has a soft lighter background, a accent marker at its start edge and a accent icon.
- **Phone and tablet:** a green top bar with a menu button, the logo mark and the company name in serif. The same menu slides in from the reading start.
- The menu is built from the user's permissions, so a screen with no permission is not in it. Sections with no visible screen disappear.
- Page content sits in a `max-w-[1500px]` container with `space-y-6`. Pages return a fragment, never their own `<main>`.

## Page anatomy

1. `PageHeader`: optional accent-ringed icon, a small accent label above the title, the serif title, a one-line description, the screen's main actions at the far end, and a fine rule with a diamond underneath. No box around it.
2. Content in white cards on the paper canvas.
3. Pop-up windows for anything that is not the main task: pick a category, print settings, item details, confirmations.

Pop-ups use `Dialog` with `DialogTitleBlock` (accent-ringed icon, serif title, description) at the top and `DialogFooter` at the bottom. They sit in the middle of the screen over a blurred green-tinted backdrop. In the footer the **secondary action comes first in the code and the primary last**, so the primary sits at the end of the row in both languages.

### Dashboard

The first screen after login. A greeting by time of day in the user's language with the long date as the label, the refresh button and update time at the far end, four `StatTile`s (total weight, boxes, different items, need attention), then one `WarehouseCard` per warehouse from Priority: name and code, the weight in large serif numerals, box and item chips, a segmented bar (in date, expiring soon, expired) with a legend, and the items that need attention grouped with their box counts. The window for "expiring soon" is `DEFAULT_ALERT_DAYS` (7) until step 9 adds the per-category setting.

### Administration

One page, two tabs under the header (accent underline on the active one): **Users** and **Activity log**. A tab shows only to people holding its permissions.

- **Users:** one card with the title, the count and the "New user" button, then a table: monogram in a green circle, name and email, job title, status badges (owner, active or disabled, must change password, each with an icon), last sign-in, and a three-dot menu (edit and permissions, reset password, disable or enable, delete). On a phone the badges move under the name so the menu always fits. Each entry opens a pop-up; reset, disable and delete ask first, and a new or reset password is shown once in a accent-framed pop-up with a copy button.
- **Permission editor** (inside the user pop-up): one row per screen with a three-way control (no access, view only, everything). The arrow opens the single actions; ticking an action also ticks "view", and an in-between state reads "Custom, n of m allowed". Devices are two switches. On a phone each row stacks, name on top and the control full width below.
- **Activity log:** a filter card (user, action, from, to; plain GET form so a filtered view can be bookmarked), then the table newest first, 25 per page with previous and next. Dates read left to right (`DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM`) even inside Hebrew. Entries are read only.

### Settings

A stack of cards, each shown only to people with its permission. **Company logo:** three tiles (light logo on green, dark logo on paper, the mark) each with an Original or Replaced badge, "Upload new" and "Restore original"; the page reloads after a change so the menu and login show it. **Priority connection:** a definition list (mode badge, address, user, password saved or not), the note that the live connection arrives in phase 6, a "Test connection" button with an inline result and an "Edit connection" pop-up. **Stand-in control:** three option tiles (Normal, Slow, Not answering) with a accent border on the chosen one, and chips with how much sample data the stand-in holds. **When Priority does not answer**, a screen shows a calm warning card (cloud-off icon, plain sentence, a retry button), never an error page; the dashboard is the model. **Coming next:** dashed, muted cards for sections later phases build, each with a "Phase n" badge. Use `SectionCard` for any new placeholder.

### Welcome (login)

One box, the same on every device. From the top: a dark band with a faint diamond lattice (`.lattice`), a double accent frame and the light logo; the language button at the reading end; the form card; the app name in small type. On a phone the box fills the screen. On a larger screen the identical box (27rem wide, rounded `3xl`, soft shadow) sits in the middle of the page on a slightly darker paper tone. It is never stretched across the width and never split into halves. The same box serves login and change password.

## Language and direction

- The UI is fully Hebrew (RTL) or fully English (LTR), never mixed. The language comes from the user's saved choice (cookie before login) and is applied once on the `<html>` element as `lang` and `dir`, plus Base UI's `DirectionProvider`.
- Every visible string goes through next-intl: `useTranslations()` in client components, `getTranslations()` in server components. Messages live in `messages/he.json` and `messages/en.json`; both files always have the same keys and TypeScript checks them against `en.json`.
- ESLint fails on text literals inside JSX (`react/jsx-no-literals`). Punctuation and symbols are allowed. The English-only `/design` page is exempt.
- Data from Priority (item names, warehouse names, categories) and label content are rendered exactly as received and are never translated or reshaped.

## Logical CSS only

The layout mirrors by itself, so physical sides are banned in `src/` (ESLint rule `no-restricted-syntax`, with `src/components/ui` exempt):

| Instead of                   | Use                           |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `ml-*`, `mr-*`               | `ms-*`, `me-*`                |
| `pl-*`, `pr-*`               | `ps-*`, `pe-*`                |
| `left-*`, `right-*`          | `start-*`, `end-*`            |
| `text-left`, `text-right`    | `text-start`, `text-end`      |
| `rounded-l-*`, `rounded-r-*` | `rounded-s-*`, `rounded-e-*`  |
| `border-l-*`, `border-r-*`   | `border-s-*`, `border-e-*`    |
| `space-x-*`                  | `gap-*` on a flex/grid parent |

Icons that imply direction get `rtl:-scale-x-100` / `rtl:rotate-180`. `Sheet` takes `side="start"` or `"end"`. Gradients that run along the reading direction use `bg-linear-to-r rtl:bg-linear-to-l`.

## Formats

The same in both languages, from `src/lib/i18n/format.ts`:

- Dates `DD/MM/YYYY`, times `HH:MM` (24h), both in `Asia/Jerusalem`. The only dates written out in words are the dashboard greeting's long date.
- Latin digits everywhere. Weights with two decimals (`14.02`), integers with thousands separators (`1,402`).
- Native `<input type="date">` follows the browser's locale, so it can show `MM/DD/YYYY`. Phase 2 replaces it with a date field that always shows `DD/MM/YYYY`.

## Logo

`public/brand/`: `logo.png` (black and red, for light backgrounds), `logo-light.png` (ivory and coral on transparent, for the green), `logo-mark.png` (the red A, for the collapsed menu and phone bar). They are the factory's own artwork. Step 9 adds the upload in settings that replaces them.

## Components

- shadcn/ui on Base UI with the RTL preset (`components.json` has `rtl: true`). Add components with `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <name>`.
- The files in `src/components/ui` **are customised in place** for this design (sizes, radii, colours, the `dark`, `soft`, `success`, `warning`, `info` variants, the blurred pop-up backdrop). Re-adding a component with `--overwrite` would undo that, so review the diff first.
- App components live in `src/components`; screen-specific pieces next to their route under `src/app`.
- Buttons that render a link need `nativeButton={false}` (Base UI warns otherwise).
````

### FILE: `README.md`

````markdown
# Factory Weighing System

Browser app that sits beside Priority: weighs boxes on a connected scale, prints barcode labels, and sends each box to Priority as its own line.

## Stack

Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui (Base UI, RTL), next-intl, PostgreSQL with Drizzle, Better Auth.

## Run locally

Requirements: Node 22+ and pnpm (`npm i -g pnpm`).

```bash
pnpm install
cp .env.example .env.local
pnpm dev
```

With no `DATABASE_URL` the app uses an embedded Postgres (PGlite) stored in `./data/pglite`. `pnpm dev` (`scripts/dev.mjs`) runs that database in its own process (`pglite-server`, port 54329) and starts Next.js against it, because `next dev` serves pages and API routes from two processes and a PGlite folder can only be opened by one. `pnpm start` is a single process and opens the folder itself.

To use a real Postgres instead, run `docker compose up -d`, set `DATABASE_URL` in `.env.local` and start the app with `pnpm dev:app` (plain `next dev`; `pnpm dev` always uses PGlite).

On every server start the app applies pending migrations and runs the idempotent seed (`src/instrumentation.ts`): the owner account from `SEED_OWNER_*` when there are no users yet, default settings, and the Priority stand-in's sample items, warehouses, orders and boxes when the stand-in is empty. Delete `./data/pglite` to start over.

## Database

- Schema: `src/server/db/schema.ts` (Drizzle). Column names are snake_case in the database, camelCase in code.
- After changing the schema run `pnpm db:generate` to write a migration into `src/server/db/migrations`, and commit it.
- Sample data for the Priority stand-in lives in `db/seed/priority/*.json`; boxes are generated relative to today's date.

`pnpm-workspace.yaml` pins `@swc/core` to 1.16.0: newer releases refuse to load on Windows machines whose user folders carry extra ACL entries (error `ERR_SWC_NATIVE_CACHE`). The comment there explains when the pin can go.

## Scripts

| Script              | What it does                                                                              |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm dev`          | Development server at `localhost:3000`, with the embedded database in its own process     |
| `pnpm dev:app`      | Plain `next dev`, for a real Postgres in `DATABASE_URL`                                   |
| `pnpm e2e`          | Playwright tests on a production build (`E2E_DEV=1` runs them against `pnpm dev`'s setup) |
| `pnpm build`        | Production build                                                                          |
| `pnpm start`        | Serve the production build                                                                |
| `pnpm lint`         | ESLint                                                                                    |
| `pnpm typecheck`    | Generate route types and run `tsc`                                                        |
| `pnpm format`       | Prettier (write)                                                                          |
| `pnpm format:check` | Prettier (check only)                                                                     |
| `pnpm test`         | Unit tests (Vitest)                                                                       |
| `pnpm db:generate`  | Write a migration from schema changes                                                     |
| `pnpm db:migrate`   | Apply migrations                                                                          |
| `pnpm db:seed`      | Migrate, then run the idempotent seed                                                     |
| `pnpm db:studio`    | Drizzle Studio (data browser)                                                             |
````

````ts
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { E2E_OWNER } from "./constants";
import { signIn } from "./helpers";

// Runs first: the seed password is still in place, so the owner's first login is the forced change.

test("login page is Hebrew and right to left by default", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/login");
  await expect(page.locator("html")).toHaveAttribute("lang", "he");
  await expect(page.locator("html")).toHaveAttribute("dir", "rtl");
});

test("the password is shown only while the eye is pressed and held", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/login");
  const box = page.locator("#password");
  await box.fill("secret-123");
  await expect(box).toHaveAttribute("type", "password");
  const eye = page.getByTestId("reveal-password");
  await eye.hover();
  await page.mouse.down();
  await expect(box).toHaveAttribute("type", "text");
  await expect(box).toHaveValue("secret-123");
  await page.mouse.up();
  await expect(box).toHaveAttribute("type", "password");
});

test("a wrong password is refused", async ({ page }) => {
  await signIn(page, E2E_OWNER.email, "not-the-password");
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login/);
  // The exact message, not only the URL: a form that was never sent also stays on the login page,
  // and a generic "sign-in failed" would mean the request itself broke.
  await expect(
    page.getByRole("alert").filter({ hasText: "האימייל או הסיסמה שגויים" }),
  ).toBeVisible();
});

test("the seeded owner must choose a new password on first login", async ({ page }) => {
  await signIn(page, E2E_OWNER.email, E2E_OWNER.password);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/change-password/);
});

test("a signed-out visitor is sent to the login page", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/inventory");
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login/);
});
````

### FILE: `e2e/02-accounts.spec.ts`

````ts
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { E2E_OWNER, OWNER_NEW_PASSWORD, USER_NEW_PASSWORD } from "./constants";
import {
  choosePassword,
  createUser,
  signIn,
  signInAsOwner,
  signOut,
  ensureEnglish,
} from "./helpers";

test.describe.configure({ mode: "serial" });

test("the owner replaces the seed password and reaches the dashboard", async ({ page }) => {
  await signIn(page, E2E_OWNER.email, E2E_OWNER.password);
  await choosePassword(page, E2E_OWNER.password, OWNER_NEW_PASSWORD);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);
});

test("a new user must change the temporary password, then sees only the screens they were given", async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  const temporary = await createUser(page, {
    name: "Dana Dashboard",
    email: "dana@e2e.test",
    screens: { Dashboard: "View only" },
    desktop: true,
    phone: true,
  });
  await signOut(page);

  await signIn(page, "dana@e2e.test", temporary);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/change-password/);

  // Mismatched confirmation is refused.
  // The temporary password is not asked for again after signing in with it.
  await expect(page.locator("#currentPassword")).toHaveCount(0);
  await page.locator("#newPassword").fill(USER_NEW_PASSWORD);
  await page.locator("#confirmPassword").fill("something-else-entirely");
  await page.locator("button[type=submit]").click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("alert").filter({ hasText: "do not match" })).toBeVisible();

  // The form clears itself after a refused attempt; fill it again only once the answer is in.
  await choosePassword(page, temporary, USER_NEW_PASSWORD);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);
  await ensureEnglish(page);

  const menu = page.getByRole("navigation", { name: "Main navigation" });
  await expect(menu.getByRole("link", { name: "Dashboard" })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(menu.getByRole("link", { name: "Inventory management" })).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(menu.getByRole("link", { name: "System administration" })).toHaveCount(0);

  // The hidden screen is "not found", not "forbidden".
  await page.goto("/inventory");
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Page not found" })).toBeVisible();
  await page.goto("/admin");
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Page not found" })).toBeVisible();
});

test("resetting a password signs the user out on their other browser", async ({
  page,
  browser,
}) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  const temporary = await createUser(page, {
    name: "Rafi Reset",
    email: "rafi@e2e.test",
    screens: { Dashboard: "View only" },
    desktop: true,
    phone: false,
  });

  // Rafi signs in on a second browser and finishes the first-login change.
  const other = await browser.newContext();
  const rafi = await other.newPage();
  await signIn(rafi, "rafi@e2e.test", temporary);
  await choosePassword(rafi, temporary, USER_NEW_PASSWORD);
  await expect(rafi).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);

  // The owner resets Rafi's password.
  await page.goto("/admin");
  const card = page.getByTestId("user-card").filter({ hasText: "Rafi Reset" });
  // Each user's card shows the screens they may open and the devices they may use.
  await expect(card.getByTestId("user-screens")).toBeVisible();
  await expect(card.getByTestId("user-devices")).toBeVisible();
  await card.getByRole("button", { name: "Actions for Rafi Reset" }).click();
  await page.getByRole("menuitem", { name: "Reset password" }).click();
  await page.getByRole("dialog").getByRole("button", { name: /Reset/ }).last().click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "I gave it to the user" })).toBeVisible();

  // Rafi's old session is gone at once.
  await rafi.goto("/dashboard");
  await expect(rafi).toHaveURL(/\/login/);
  await other.close();
});

test("a user with history is deleted only after a warning, and the history stays", async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  const temporary = await createUser(page, {
    name: "Gil Gone",
    email: "gil@e2e.test",
    screens: { Dashboard: "View only" },
    desktop: true,
    phone: true,
  });
  // Gil signs in, which is history in the activity log.
  await page.context().clearCookies();
  await signIn(page, "gil@e2e.test", temporary);
  await choosePassword(page, temporary, USER_NEW_PASSWORD);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);
  await page.context().clearCookies();

  await signInAsOwner(page);
  await page.goto("/admin");
  const card = page.getByTestId("user-card").filter({ hasText: "Gil Gone" });
  await card.getByRole("button", { name: "Actions for Gil Gone" }).click();
  await page.getByRole("menuitem", { name: "Delete user" }).click();
  const dialog = page.getByRole("dialog");
  await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Delete", exact: true }).click();

  // The warning: the user stays until it is confirmed again.
  await expect(dialog.getByTestId("history-warning")).toContainText("has history in the system");
  await expect(card).toBeVisible();
  await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Cancel" }).click();
  await expect(card).toBeVisible();

  await card.getByRole("button", { name: "Actions for Gil Gone" }).click();
  await page.getByRole("menuitem", { name: "Delete user" }).click();
  await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Delete", exact: true }).click();
  await expect(dialog.getByTestId("history-warning")).toBeVisible();
  await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Delete anyway" }).click();
  await expect(page.getByText("User deleted")).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByTestId("user-card").filter({ hasText: "Gil Gone" })).toHaveCount(0);

  // His history is still in the activity log, under his name.
  await page.goto("/admin?tab=log");
  await expect(page.getByText("Gil").first()).toBeVisible();
});
````

### FILE: `e2e/05-language-and-layout.spec.ts`

````ts
import { expect, test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
import { signIn, signInAsOwner, signOut } from "./helpers";
import { E2E_OWNER, OWNER_NEW_PASSWORD } from "./constants";

test.describe.configure({ mode: "serial" });

const SCREENS = [
  "/dashboard",
  "/catalog",
  "/receiving",
  "/vendor-receiving",
  "/inventory",
  "/settings",
  "/admin",
];

async function expectNoSideScroll(page: Page) {
  const overflow = await page.evaluate(
    () => document.documentElement.scrollWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth,
  );
  expect(overflow).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0);
}

test("the language choice switches direction and survives sign-out and sign-in", async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page); // English, left to right
  await expect(page.locator("html")).toHaveAttribute("dir", "ltr");

  await page.getByTitle("עברית").click();
  await expect(page.locator("html")).toHaveAttribute("lang", "he");
  await expect(page.locator("html")).toHaveAttribute("dir", "rtl");

  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "יציאה" }).first().click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login/);
  await page.context().clearCookies(); // only the saved user choice may bring the language back

  await signIn(page, E2E_OWNER.email, OWNER_NEW_PASSWORD);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);
  await expect(page.locator("html")).toHaveAttribute("lang", "he");
  await expect(page.locator("html")).toHaveAttribute("dir", "rtl");

  await page.getByTitle("English").click();
  await expect(page.locator("html")).toHaveAttribute("dir", "ltr");
  await signOut(page);
});

for (const [label, size] of [
  ["phone", { width: 375, height: 812 }],
  ["desktop", { width: 1280, height: 800 }],
] as const) {
  test(`every screen fits the ${label} width in both languages`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.setViewportSize(size);
    await page.goto("/login");
    await expectNoSideScroll(page);

    await signIn(page, E2E_OWNER.email, OWNER_NEW_PASSWORD);
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);

    // The owner is in English here. Hebrew first, then back to English so the next test starts the same.
    for (const lang of ["he", "en"] as const) {
      // The button sits in the side menu: always on screen on a desktop, behind the menu button on a phone.
      const switchButton = page
        .locator(`button[title="${lang === "he" ? "עברית" : "English"}"]:visible`)
        .first();
      if (!(await switchButton.isVisible())) {
        await page
          .getByRole("button", { name: lang === "he" ? "Open the menu" : "פתיחת התפריט" })
          .click();
      }
      await switchButton.click();
      await expect(page.locator("html")).toHaveAttribute("lang", lang);
      const dir = lang === "he" ? "rtl" : "ltr";
      for (const path of SCREENS) {
        await page.goto(path);
        await expect(page.locator("html")).toHaveAttribute("dir", dir);
        await expectNoSideScroll(page);
      }
    }
  });
}
````

### FILE: `e2e/06-activity-log.spec.ts`

````ts
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { USER_NEW_PASSWORD } from "./constants";
import { ensureEnglish, signIn, signInAsOwner } from "./helpers";

// Runs after the earlier specs, so the log already holds their sign-ins, user creations and reset.

test("the owner sees what happened, with who did it and from which device", async ({ page }) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  await page.goto("/admin?tab=log");
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Activity log" })).toBeVisible();

  // The log holds 25 entries a page, so look each action up through its filter.
  for (const [key, label] of [
    ["auth.login", "Signed in"],
    ["auth.loginFailed", "Failed sign-in"],
    ["auth.passwordChanged", "Changed password"],
    ["admin.userCreated", "Created a user"],
    ["admin.passwordReset", "Reset a password"],
  ]) {
    await page.goto(`/admin?tab=log&action=${key}`);
    await expect(page.getByRole("row", { name: new RegExp(label) }).first()).toBeVisible();
  }

  // An owner's action carries the owner's name and the device it came from.
  await page.goto("/admin?tab=log&action=admin.userCreated");
  const created = page.getByRole("row", { name: /Created a user/ }).first();
  await expect(created).toContainText("E2E Owner");
  // The device column is an icon (monitor for a desktop) with the device named for screen readers.
  await expect(created.locator("svg.lucide-monitor")).toBeVisible();
  await expect(created).toContainText("Desktop");
});

test("the log is printed as a report of every entry that matches the filters", async ({ page }) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    window.print = () => {
      const root = document.getElementById("report-print-root");
      (window as unknown as { __report: string }).__report = root?.innerText ?? "";
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event("afterprint"));
    };
  });
  await page.goto("/admin?tab=log&action=admin.userCreated");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Print report" }).click();
  await expect
    .poll(() => page.evaluate(() => (window as unknown as { __report?: string }).__report ?? ""))
    .toContain("Created a user");
  const report = await page.evaluate(() => (window as unknown as { __report: string }).__report);
  expect(report).toContain("Activity log");
  expect(report).toContain("E2E Owner");
  // Only what the filter keeps is in it.
  expect(report).not.toContain("Failed sign-in");
});

test("a user without the log permission cannot open it", async ({ page }) => {
  await signIn(page, "dana@e2e.test", USER_NEW_PASSWORD);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);
  await ensureEnglish(page);
  await page.goto("/admin?tab=log");
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Page not found" })).toBeVisible();
});
````

````ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { USER_NEW_PASSWORD } from "./constants";
import { choosePassword, createUser, ensureEnglish, signIn, signInAsOwner } from "./helpers";

interface SeedItem {
  partname: string;
  partdes: string;
  epartdes: string;
  barcode: string;
  familydes: string;
  expiredays: number;
}

// The stand-in's catalog is this seed file, so the expectations come from it.
const seed: SeedItem[] = JSON.parse(readFileSync("db/seed/priority/items.json", "utf8"));
const total = (n: number) => `Total shown: ${n}`;
// The same alphabetical order the screen uses: Hebrew letters in order, numbers by value.
const abc = new Intl.Collator("he", { numeric: true, sensitivity: "base" });
const byName = (a: SeedItem, b: SeedItem) =>
  abc.compare(a.partdes, b.partdes) || abc.compare(a.partname, b.partname);

test.describe.configure({ mode: "serial" });

test("the owner sees every category as a card, and every item under its category", async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  await page.goto("/catalog");
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Item catalog" })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole("status")).toHaveText(total(seed.length));

  // A card for all categories, then one per category with its count.
  const categories = [...new Set(seed.map((i) => i.familydes))];
  const group = page.getByRole("group", { name: "Categories" });
  await expect(group.getByRole("button")).toHaveCount(categories.length + 1);
  await expect(group.getByRole("button").first()).toContainText("All categories");

  // Every item is a card in its category's section, with both names and the item number.
  const sections = page.getByTestId("catalog-section");
  await expect(sections).toHaveCount(categories.length);
  const first = seed[0];
  const section = page.getByRole("region", { name: first.familydes, exact: true });
  const card = section.getByRole("button", { name: `Open ${first.partdes}` });
  await expect(card).toContainText(first.partname);
  await expect(card).toContainText(first.epartdes);
  await expect(section.getByRole("button", { name: /^Open / })).toHaveCount(
    seed.filter((i) => i.familydes === first.familydes).length,
  );
});

test("categories, and the items in each, are in alphabetical order", async ({ page }) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  await page.goto("/catalog");

  // The category cards after "All categories", and the sections, follow the alphabet.
  const categories = [...new Set(seed.map((i) => i.familydes))].sort(abc.compare);
  const cards = page.getByRole("group", { name: "Categories" }).getByRole("button");
  const names = (await cards.allInnerTexts()).slice(1).map((text) => text.split("\n")[0].trim());
  expect(names).toEqual(categories);
  const headings = (await page.getByTestId("catalog-section").locator("h2").allInnerTexts()).map(
    (text) => text.trim(),
  );
  expect(headings).toEqual(categories);

  // Inside every section the items follow the alphabet of their names.
  for (const category of categories) {
    const expected = seed
      .filter((i) => i.familydes === category)
      .sort(byName)
      .map((i) => `Open ${i.partdes}`);
    const shown = await page
      .getByRole("region", { name: category, exact: true })
      .getByRole("button", { name: /^Open / })
      .evaluateAll((buttons) => buttons.map((b) => b.getAttribute("aria-label")));
    expect(shown).toEqual(expected);
  }
});

test("a category opens a window with its items, and an item there opens the item", async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  await page.goto("/catalog");
  const category = seed[0].familydes;
  const inCategory = seed.filter((i) => i.familydes === category).sort(byName);

  await page
    .getByRole("group", { name: "Categories" })
    .getByRole("button", { name: new RegExp(`of ${category}$`) })
    .click();
  const dialog = page.getByRole("dialog");
  await expect(
    dialog.getByRole("heading", { name: `Items in the category: ${category}` }),
  ).toBeVisible();
  await expect(dialog).toContainText(
    `${inCategory.length === 1 ? "One item" : `${inCategory.length} items`} found in this category.`,
  );
  const cards = dialog.getByTestId("category-items").getByRole("button");
  await expect(cards).toHaveCount(inCategory.length);
  await expect(cards.first()).toContainText(`#${inCategory[0].partname}`);

  // Opening an item there shows the item instead.
  await cards.first().click();
  await expect(
    page.getByRole("dialog").getByRole("heading", { name: inCategory[0].partdes }),
  ).toBeVisible();
  await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
  await expect(page.getByRole("dialog")).toHaveCount(0); // both windows have finished closing

  // The window also closes with its own button.
  await page
    .getByRole("group", { name: "Categories" })
    .getByRole("button", { name: new RegExp(`of ${category}$`) })
    .click();
  await page.getByRole("dialog").getByRole("button", { name: "Close window" }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("dialog")).toHaveCount(0); // both windows have finished closing
});

test("search finds items by name, ignoring case, and says when nothing matches", async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  await page.goto("/catalog");
  const word = seed[0].epartdes.split(" ")[0].toUpperCase();
  const found = seed.filter((i) => i.epartdes.toLowerCase().includes(word.toLowerCase()));
  const search = page.getByRole("searchbox", { name: "Search the catalog" });
  await search.fill(word);
  await expect(page.getByRole("status")).toHaveText(total(found.length));
  await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: /^Open / })).toHaveCount(found.length);

  await search.fill("no-such-item-anywhere");
  await expect(page.getByText("No item matches.")).toBeVisible();
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Show all items" }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("status")).toHaveText(total(seed.length));

  // The "all categories" card also brings everything back.
  await search.fill(word);
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: /^All categories/ }).click();
  await expect(search).toHaveValue("");
  await expect(page.getByRole("status")).toHaveText(total(seed.length));
});

test("an item opens to Priority's fields, with a way to print its label", async ({ page }) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  await page.goto("/catalog");
  const first = seed[0];
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: `Open ${first.partdes}` }).click();

  const dialog = page.getByRole("dialog");
  await expect(dialog.getByRole("heading", { name: first.partdes })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(dialog).toContainText(first.partname);
  await expect(dialog).toContainText(first.barcode);
  await expect(dialog).toContainText(first.epartdes);
  await expect(dialog).toContainText(`${first.expiredays} days`);
  await expect(dialog).toContainText("Items are edited only in Priority.");

  // Printing happens in the same window, and cancelling it goes back to the details.
  await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Print a label" }).click();
  await expect(dialog.getByRole("heading", { name: "Print item label" })).toBeVisible();
  await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Cancel" }).click();
  await expect(dialog.getByRole("heading", { name: first.partdes })).toBeVisible();

  await dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Close", exact: true }).first().click();
  await expect(dialog).toBeHidden();
});

test("a user allowed to see the catalog but not details or printing gets boxes that do not open", async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await signInAsOwner(page);
  const temporary = await createUser(page, {
    name: "Cleo Catalog",
    email: "cleo@e2e.test",
    screens: { "Item catalog": "View only" },
    desktop: true,
    phone: false,
  });
  await page.context().clearCookies();

  await signIn(page, "cleo@e2e.test", temporary);
  await choosePassword(page, temporary, USER_NEW_PASSWORD);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/catalog/);
  await ensureEnglish(page);

  await expect(page.getByRole("status")).toHaveText(total(seed.length));
  await expect(page.getByText(seed[0].partdes).first()).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: /^Open / })).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(page.getByText("click a box")).toHaveCount(0);
});
````
